text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic meets Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic and ownership transformation minister Milan Beko, says work on reform laws is going well, parliament will discuss the concessions bill Tuesday and the public debate on the ownership transformation bill will soon be completed.
- Serbian president Zoran Lilic congratulates Yugoslav security bodies on May 13 Security Day for safeguarding the citizens and the territory of the country.
- U.S. Charge d'Affaires Richard Miles says the U.S. supports Yugoslavia's integration in Europe and the world.
- The Slovenian company Smelt makes first flight Ljubljana-Belgrade since 1991 on Monday. The line will be flown by a seven-passenger Cessna plane.
- Turnover in stores reduced by half this year in relation to 1996, says president of Serbian traders' union Relja Dabic.

- The draft amendment to the communication law adopted by the Serbian government lays down regulations for separating the post from the telecommunications in the PTT system and for sale of part of the company capital, paper learns unofficially.
- Chinese businessmen visit Yugoslav chamber of commerce. Trade with China in 1996 stood at $60 million and in the first quarter of 1997 $21 million.

- Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic opens international technics fair, welcomes numerous foreign participants and says the federal government will develop a stable political, economic and legal framework for promotion of economic cooperation.
- Benetton to open eight new stores in Serbia by end of 1997 in cooperation with Serbian firm Ktitor.
NASA BORBA
- Health workers in Serbia on strike over late wages, emergency service, and five other institutions remain open. Serbian government to submit a proposal Wednesday.
- Talks on succession of former Yugoslavia scheduled for June 2-4 in Brussels by international mediator Sir Arthur Watts.

- The problem of over two billion dinars of debts owed by agriculture combines and cooperatives to commercial banks should be turned into a public debt, says director of Institute for agriculture economics Dusan Radmanovic.
- Bank for International Settlements (BIS) invites former Yugoslav republics - Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Macedonia to become members, but excludes Yugoslavia.
- Humanitarian organisation Caritas opens soup kitchens in Serbia's southern town of Nis, providing 1,000 meals a day.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Yugoslav firms' internal debts have reached close to 10 billion dinars, estimates Institute of Economic Sciences.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- International mediator for the succession of ex-Yugoslavia Sir Arthur Watts asked Belgrade to agree immediately to the division of diplomatic offices of the former Yugoslavia abroad during his visit to Belgrade ten days ago, sources say.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic was unanimously re-elected Deputy President of the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists at Monday session of the DPS Main Board.
- DPS main board upheld legality of party statute provision on DPS approval of the composiiton of the government.
The Montenegrin University demands that the state leadership respect the law in resolving the current disagreements and that the media provide full and unbiased information.
- Unlimited imports of steel products hit Niksic steel mill very hard, reducing its output in the first two months of 1997 to 11,000 tonnes, down from the 19,000 planned.

- A joint venture involving Resource International, a British-Cypriot company, and Montenegro's regional coastal waterworks is expected to resolve the garbage disposal problem according to the highest standards. -- Belgrade newsroom + 381 11 222 4305
